newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians hope U.S. envoy will be honest broker.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians hope U.S. envoy will be honest broker.

text.p: A top Palestinian negotiator said he hoped American Middle East envoy Dennis Ross would not favour Israel on his return later on Saturday to push forward talks on Hebron.
Ross, who failed in October to broker an accord on Israel's partial withdrawal from Hebron in the West Bank, is due to meet Palestinians on Saturday and Israelis on Sunday.
"We want him (Ross) to be on the side of the agreement, not on the side of Israel," PLO official Hassan Asfour told Reuters.
In Hebron, clashes broke out between Arabs and Israeli settlers and troops. Palestinians said the soldiers beat several demonstrators and two were rushed to a hospital.

U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher's comments on Thursday that Palestinians had to make concessions on Hebron irked PLO leaders. An Israeli legislator who met with Yasser Arafat said the Palestinian president wanted Ross replaced.
The United States, sponsor of Israeli-Arab peace talks launched in 1991, has pressed Israelis and Palestinians to finalise their accord on Hebron and move on to negotiations on an overall peace deal.

"He (Arafat) said he's ready for mediation or arbitration as long as it is not done by Dennis Ross," said Yossi Beilin, a key figure in peace talks that led to the breakthrough Israel-PLO peace in 1993.

Beilin, whose Labour party was ousted by hardline Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in elections last May, met Arafat in the Gaza Strip on Friday. He said the Palestinian leader did not explain his objection to Ross.

"I said to him that that would be his biggest mistake, that the United States is the sponsor and Dennis Ross is its representative and even if he would like to have others, the best thing that he could do is to accept Ross as a mediator because that's the only way to make progress in the Hebron talks," Beilin told Reuters.
A PLO official said Ross would go to Gaza upon landing in Israel to see Arafat late on Saturday. He would hold talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu early on Sunday.

The U.S. administration last sent Ross after clashes in September in the West Bank and Gaza killed 15 Israeli soldiers and 60 Palestinians. He left after his three-week mediation effort collapsed but said the sides had narrowed the gaps.

Christopher had put the onus for progress on Arafat on Thursday, saying Israel had "made some moves" over Hebron and it was up to the Palestinians to respond. He also announced the return of Ross to Israel.
Arafat, who says there has been no progress, said on Friday: "The most important thing is that Mr Ross has to be an accurate mediator and not to be biased on the side of Israel."
Israelis and Palestinians accuse each other of foot-dragging in talks on Hebron.

Arafat has demanded Israel implement the partial withdrawal agreement it signed more than a year ago. Netanyahu has sought changes to protect around 400 militant Jewish settlers living among 100,000 Arabs in the town.
Hundreds of Arabs gathered in central Hebron on Saturday after Jewish settlers scuffled with Palestinian school children in the town, a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence.
Soldiers intervened, arresting at least two Palestinians and clearing demonstrators from the approach to one of the Jewish enclaves in Hebron.
